chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Walad, from Humran, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
Ẓihār does not occur through an oath, nor in a case of harm, nor in a state of anger. Ẓihār is only valid upon a state of purity, without intercourse, with the testimony of two Muslim witnesses.

key_terms.طُهْرٍ: ritual purity, here meaning a period of purity from menstruation
key_terms.ظِهَارٌ: Ẓihār, a pre-Islamic form of declaring one's wife unlawful by likening her to a prohibited female relative
key_terms.مُسْلِمَيْنِ: two Muslim men serving as witnesses

ai.seo_question: When is ẓihār valid according to Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith sets legal conditions for the validity of ẓihār in Islamic family law. It states that ẓihār is not valid when uttered as an oath, in a harmful manner, or in anger, and it is only valid when pronounced during a state of purity without prior intercourse and before two Muslim witnesses.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4845 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Walad, from Humran, from Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), who said:

"Ẓihar (a form of divorce by comparison) does not occur through an oath, nor in a case of harm, nor in a state of anger. Ẓihar is only valid when it is declared during a state of purity (from menstruation), without prior intercourse, and in the presence of two Muslim witnesses."
